definition: A relation network (RN) is an artificial neural network component with a structure that can reason about relations among objects.
details: An example category of such relations is spatial relations (above, below, left, right, in front of, behind). RNs can infer relations, they are data efficient, and they operate on a set of objects without regard to the objects' order.

explainer.lead: A neural network component whose structure reasons about relations among objects, rather than about each object alone. It is data efficient and operates on a set of objects irrespective of their order.

tiers.eli5: Show it a handful of shapes and it can tell you which is above, below or in front of which — order of the items doesn't matter.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it as a module on pairs of object features to score spatial or pairwise relations. The pitfall is that pairwise scoring grows combinatorially with the number of objects.
tiers.paperLevel: Objects are embedded, then a relation module scores each ordered pair, typically aggregating pairwise outputs. It is order-invariant over the input set; limits include quadratic cost in object count.

explainer.example: Given coordinates of several objects, it outputs relations such as 'A above B' and 'C behind D' for each pair.
